Acetylation of treha-lose mycolates is essential for efficient membrane transport in Cory-nebacterineae.

In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the regulation of membrane transport of mycolic acid-containing glycolipids in the genus Corynebacterinum, which is a model for the related pathogen M. tuberculosis.
the synthesis of the cell envelope of Corynebacteriaceae.
the identification of novel cell wall biosynthesis enzymes that are required for efficient membrane transport of mycolates in Corynebacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the acetylation of trehalse mycolates is essential to the transport of the trehalose myclocates across the inner membrane in the Corynebacterinaceae.
acetylation of trehalsome monomycolates is required to enable efficient MmpL3-mediated transport of these lipids across the inner membrane.
acetylation of TMCM by NCgl2759 (TmaT), is required for MmpL-mediated export and is an important regulatory step in the biosynthesis of the Corynebacteriaceae cell envelope.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TmaT is an essential enzyme for the synthesis of the mycolic acids that are the major cell wall components of Corynebacteria and Mycobacteria.
TmaT is required for efficient transport of TMCM to the periplasim and that this process requires a mycolyl moietyl group on TMCM.
TmaT is a novel TM CM acetylatransferase that regulates transport of TMM across the inner membrane of Corynebacteriaceae.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acetylation of trehaose mycolates by TmaT is required for their efficient transport by MmpL transporters.
the acetylation of trehalse mycolates is a regulatory mechanism that is required for efficient transport of these glycolipids across the cell membrane.

acetylation of mycolic acid is a key post-translational modification required for efficient transport of mycolylated glycolipids in Corynebactineae, and is therefore an attractive target for the development of new antimicrobial agents.
